display.title: Episode 122: Rabbi Akiva and the Jug of Water (Sefirah)
display.summary_short: A Sefirah show without music: why these are days of mourning, why water and negel vasser are so precious, and how Rabbi Akiva's washing in prison won him his freedom.
display.summary_long: Broadcast during Sefiras HaOmer 5744, the week after Pirkei Avos chapter 1 was learned. The show opens without music, and Uncle Yossi explains why: there is a time for joy and a time for sadness, and during Sefirah we hold back from celebrations because Rabbi Akiva's students, who did not show each other respect, died in a plague that ended on Lag BaOmer. We should check that we honor others and build Ahavas Yisroel and achdus. An eleven-year-old guest recites the Shema. Uncle Yossi then speaks about water, Hashem's precious gift, and its power of purity, the reason we wash negel vasser every morning. The story follows: Rabbi Akiva, jailed for teaching Torah and given no water for three days, uses his jug to wash his hands with a brachah instead of drinking. The amazed ruler frees him and makes him an advisor. Uncle Yossi then teaches Rabbi Akiva's great rule, love your fellow as yourself, and from Pirkei Avos chapter 1, the humility Moshe learned from Mount Sinai. The show ends with the Lag BaOmer parade announcement.
display.lesson: Show respect and love to every Jew, and treasure every mitzvah, even at great cost, as Rabbi Akiva did.

date.note: Sefirah; Pirkei Avos chapter 1 learned 'last week'; Lag BaOmer (20 May) announced; episode 123 says 20 May is 12 days away.

advisories.note: Thousands of Rabbi Akiva's students died in a plague (explained briefly).
Teaching Torah was forbidden; Rabbi Akiva is jailed and left without water for three days.

privacy.note: Shema guest named in full with age and town.

sources_cited.note: 'Love your fellow as yourself', called by Rabbi Akiva a great rule of the Torah (cited from the Gemara).
'Moshe received the Torah from Sinai': humility learned from the lowest mountain.
